questions: Should the column shuffling be performed in-place on a copy of the input array, or should it modify the original array?
If the array has only one column, does shuffling columns have any effect, and should PCA still be performed on the single column?
Should the seed parameter control both the column shuffling and any internal randomness in sklearn's PCA (e.g., solver initialization)?
For arrays with exactly 2 columns, should PCA reduce to 2 components (i.e., no dimensionality reduction) or should it still compute 2 principal components?
If the input array contains NaN or infinite values, should the function handle them gracefully, raise an error, or let PCA fail internally?
Should the returned DataFrame have an index that matches the row indices of the original array (e.g., 0 to n_samples-1) or a default RangeIndex?
Is the column shuffling applied to the transposed array (shuffling rows of the transpose) equivalent to shuffling columns of the original array, as implied by the clarification?
Should the function standardize (center and scale) the data before applying PCA, or rely on sklearn's default which only centers?
